subject: GreenState private connectivity: operational readiness and recommended paths
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@greenstatehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: GreenState private connectivity: operational readiness and recommended paths

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the time last week. Per our discussion, I pulled together the operational checklist and a short comparison of the three typical connectivity patterns for Redwood Private deployments: VPC Peering (direct peering/transit via TGW), AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints + NLB in our account), and Site-to-Site VPN (IPSec). See attached two quick artifacts: connectivity_comparison_sheet.xlsx and network_checklist_for_private_deploy.md.

High-level tradeoffs (very short):
- VPC Peering: low-latency, low egress overhead, but requires route management and does not support transitive routing across accounts without a transit gateway. Good when both sides are in your org or you can use TGW.
- PrivateLink: strongest isolation (no cross-account route exposure), simpler security boundaries, great for strict compliance because we present an endpoint service to your VPC. Higher per-GB charges and slightly more operational setup (NLB, endpoint service).
- Site-to-Site VPN: quickest to stand up, predictable network path, but higher and variable latency, less suitable for sub-10ms SLOs. Typically used as a temporary/fallback path or for on-prem connectivity where direct cloud peering is infeasible.

Questions for the tech sync so we can recommend a final design:
- Desired P95 latency SLO for API calls to Redwood? (example: 10ms p95 internal, 30ms acceptable)
- Expected steady/peak RPS and total egress volumes per day/month
- Does GreenState require that traffic never traverse the public internet (i.e., no public endpoints)?
- Any constraints on CIDR space we need to avoid (overlap) and whether you can accept /24s on endpoint subnets?
- Who from your security/compliance team should we include to validate mTLS, audit log flows, and SOC 2 artefacts?

Next steps I propose:
1) Short engineering sync (30 mins) to confirm constraints and run a quick latency pilot in us-east-1.
2) We'll produce an operational runbook (networking + failover) and a cost delta for Peering vs PrivateLink vs VPN based on your estimated egress.

If you prefer, we can sketch two flavors of the design: PrivateLink-first (recommended for workloads with strict isolation and cross-account boundaries) or Peering-first (recommended for same-org, large steady throughput).

Available times for a technical sync: Tue 2026-08-17 14:00-16:00 ET, Wed 2026-08-18 09:00-11:00 ET.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few constraints from our side:
- Region: us-east-1 (we have some DR in us-west-2 but primary traffic will be us-east-1).
- Latency target: ideally p95 < 20ms for inference calls; sub-10ms is optimistic but would be great.
- Expected traffic: baseline ~20 RPS, peak planned ~200 RPS during batch processing windows. Monthly egress estimate ~6TB.
- Compliance: HIPAA; we need a documented path that avoids public internet for PHI in transit when possible. PrivateLink looks attractive because of the cross-account isolation requirement.
- Procurement: we'll need a simple network diagram, a short list of required IAM roles, and SOC 2 evidence for the service.

Would prefer to do the technical sync Wed 2026-08-18 09:30 ET. I'll invite our network lead and someone from security to the call.

Thanks,
Samir

Thanks Samir — Wed 09:30 ET works for us. Invites incoming.

A couple of operational notes so the sync is productive:
- Our recommendation (based on your constraints) is to prioritize PrivateLink for the production path: it avoids route exposure, simplifies least-privilege network ACLs, and aligns well with HIPAA boundary requirements since traffic terminates at an NLB we control and is carried over the AWS private endpoint.
- If GreenState prefers to keep everything within your AWS account and you can accept cross-account peering complexity, VPC Peering (option with Transit Gateway) can be more cost-efficient for sustained high throughput because it removes PrivateLink data processing and per-GB charges. However, TGW adds management overhead and may require approvals from your infra team.
- Site-to-Site VPN we suggest only as a contingency or for on-prem datacenter connectivity because latency and jitter are less predictable. Use an IPSec link with BGP for failover, and treat it as asynchronous traffic for ML batch jobs or development usage.

Operational pieces we'll bring to the call:
- A short pilot plan (3-step): create endpoint in a shadow VPC, run synthetic p95 tests, evaluate throughput limits, and validate connection handoffs (mTLS + audit log capture).
- Runbook fragments: cert rotation, endpoint lifecycle, observed failure modes, fallback to VPN, and escalation paths.

I've attached a rapid cost sketch (cost_estimate_privatelink_vpcpeering_vpn.pdf) to give procurement something to chew on before the call.

Action items for the sync:
- Samir: confirm who from security will join (so we can deep-dive mTLS/audit flows).
- Markus/Neha: we'll present the cost comparison and the runbook sketch.
- Engineering: Rishi will own mTLS certificate handling and audit log export settings; he'll produce a short runbook post-call.

—Kim

Thanks — our security lead (Marta Gomez) will join and asked two quick pre-call clarifications:
1) How does Redwood manage certificates for the PrivateLink NLB? Do you support customer-provided certs or does Redwood terminate TLS and do mTLS from the NLB to your service?
2) Where are audit logs (connection metadata) written and what retention can we provide for egress/ingest telemetry? We need at least 1 year retention available for audit purposes.

Happy to discuss on the call but wanted these on the record.

—Samir
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: GreenState private connectivity: operational readiness and recommended paths

I'll take point on the mTLS/cert flow and the audit-log retention ask. Quick notes pre-call:
- We support customer-provided certs at the NLB level (you can bring your cert or we can provision via ACM in your account). For PrivateLink we usually terminate TLS at the NLB in the provider account and then use mTLS from the NLB to the internal service; we can also configure end-to-end TLS if GreenState requires no termination on our side.
- Audit logs: connection metadata (source/dest, protocol, bytes, timestamps) can be pushed to a customer-managed S3 or to our audit pipeline; retention to 1 year is feasible — we'll document retention/export options and the minimum schema required for your auditors.
- I'll prepare a short runbook (cert rotation, endpoint lifecycle, failure remediation) and a test plan (synthetic p95 runs and throughput ramp).

I'll share the runbook and a short checklist after the call.

—Rishi
